 Gold rate today in Delhi, November 5: 24 karat climbs to ₹14,617 a gram on Dhanteras eve
 By Upstox News Desk 2 min read | Updated on November 05, 2026, 12:12 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 Gold prices in Delhi rose ₹322 a gram to ₹14,617 for 24 karat on Thursday, November 5, 2026, with 22 karat at ₹13,400 and 18 karat at ₹10,967
 Prices have increased on Dhanteras eve in the national capital. | Image: Shutterstock
 Retail gold rates in Delhi were ₹14,617 per gram for 24 karat and ₹13,400 per gram for 22 karat on Thursday, November 5, 2026 at the time of writing, as the capital's jewellers opened for their busiest morning of the season, a day before Dhanteras.
 Open FREE Demat Account within minutes! Join now 
 According to Goodreturns data, 10 grams of 24 karat gold on Dhanteras eve now costs approx. ₹1,46,170, while 22 karat, the grade most Delhi ornaments are sold in, is ₹1,34,000. Studded and machine-cut pieces are priced on the 18 karat rate at ₹10,967 a gram, or ₹1,09,670 for 10 grams.
 Purity Rate per gram Rate per 10 g Change from Nov 4 
 24K (999) ₹14,617 ₹1,46,170 +₹3,220 (+2.25%) 
 22K (916) ₹13,400 ₹1,34,000 +₹2,950 (+2.25%) 
 18K (750) ₹10,967 ₹1,09,670 +₹2,420 (+2.26%) 
 Gold rates in Delhi on November 5, 2026, indicative, before making charges and GST 
 As the festive shopping ahead of Dhanteras enters in the last phase, retailers and traders are keeping their extra staff for one more day.
 Since November 1, the capital has seen ₹49, ₹27, ₹316 and now ₹322 a gram of gains, ₹714 in all, or 5.1%. The ₹338 that October 31 took away has been recovered more than twice over, and Thursday's price print also sits above the ₹14,410 of October 29.
 Please treat the above numbers as indicative rather than final. The board you see in a shop reflects that shop's actual price position. And two stores a kilometre apart can differ by tens of rupees a gram. So buyers should check a few stores before finalising their jewellery purchase. To the carat-based price, making charges and 3% GST are added. For instance, a 10-gram 22 karat piece with 8% making charges attracts GST of ₹4,342, taking the total to about ₹1,49,062.
 Making charges can range from about 5% on plain bangles to 18% on machine-cut designs. You may negotiate this charge on the eve of the festival. You should also check that the jewellery piece you are buying is hallmarked, that its six-digit HUID matches the bill, and that weight, purity, labour and tax are printed separately.
